purpose: Primary-source snapshot for Search/localization rules that are easy to fossilize or confuse with agent-interoperability conventions.

rules.claim: Google Search does not require llms.txt and it does not positively or negatively affect Search visibility or rankings. A project may keep it for other systems that use it.
HTML, HTTP header and sitemap hreflang methods are equivalent for Google. Using all of them provides no Search benefit and increases implementation complexity.
Google hreflang uses ISO 639-1 language codes, optional ISO 15924 script and optional ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 region. Generic BCP 47 validity alone is not proof of Google hreflang eligibility.
Google determines page language primarily from visible content, not URL language tokens, html lang or hreflang. html lang remains important for accessibility, browsers and downstream tooling.
FAQ rich results no longer appear in Google Search as of 2026-05-07; FAQPage may still have non-Google semantic uses but must not be sold as a current Google rich-result optimization.

Search Console exposes Generative AI performance data for AI Overviews and AI Mode and a Search generative AI inclusion control. Owner access is required; absence of owner data is not a site implementation failure.
